itemListElement.name: How Fast Should You Gain Weight?

children: How fast should you gain weight?

For muscle-focused gain, a useful published starting range for novice and intermediate natural bodybuilders is about 0.25–0.5% of body weight per week. It is a reference point, not a promise. Training experience, starting body composition and your real response should shape the pace.
Published by Kestora Labs, the maker of BulkBro · Updated
How fast should you gain weight?
Pick a modest weekly pace, measure under consistent conditions, and judge several observations together. A faster scale increase does not guarantee faster muscle growth and can increase fat gain.
Choose the rate before the calories

A weight-gain target is easier to evaluate when it includes a pace. A narrative review of off-season nutrition for natural bodybuilders proposed roughly 0.25–0.5% of body weight per week for novice and intermediate lifters, with more advanced lifters using a more conservative approach. That range is specific to a muscle-focused training context and should not be treated as a universal medical recommendation.

For general healthy weight gain, the NHS advises gradual gain and suggests that adults could try adding around 300–500 calories per day. These are two different ways of framing a starting plan: one describes a weekly outcome, while the other describes an intake change.
See what the published range means for you
Enter your current body weight to calculate 0.25–0.5% per week. No value is stored or transmitted.
These calculations show the scale of the range. They do not predict how much of a change will be muscle, fat, fluid or food mass.
Use a trend, not a deadline

Body weight can move from day to day even when the underlying direction has not changed. Use the same scale at a similar time and compare repeated readings. A single result above or below the target pace is not enough to diagnose the plan.
It also matters whether you completed the intake target. A slow trend after averaging below the target means something different from a slow trend after a complete, consistently logged week. Read
how to track calories for weight gain
before interpreting incomplete data, and use a
Change one input at a time

A 2023 study in resistance-trained participants found that faster body-mass gain was more strongly associated with increased skinfold thickness than with better strength or muscle-thickness outcomes. The study was small, but it supports a cautious principle: a much larger surplus is not automatically a better muscle-building plan.

If the trend remains below your intended pace after consistent logging and measurement, make a measured calorie adjustment. If it is above the range, consider reducing the surplus rather than waiting for a long correction phase. BulkBro records whether the target stayed steady or changed so the next week still has a clear comparison.
Keep the goal in health context

A bodybuilding rate is not appropriate for every person. Speak with a qualified healthcare professional if your weight is low, falling unintentionally, affected by a medical condition or medication, or connected to disordered eating. People under 18 and those who are pregnant or breastfeeding need individual guidance.

acceptedAnswer.text: Both methods are used. Your workplace policy determines whether the percentage is applied to gross tips, total sales, food sales or another base.

Before taxes. Use your workplace policy to choose the correct tip-out base and rate.
Then subtract the tip-out from your gross tips. If you add wages, you can also see total earnings and what the shift paid per hour.

The important part is choosing the same base your workplace uses. Some restaurants calculate tip-out as a percentage of gross tips. Others use total sales, food sales or another sales category. A fixed dollar amount is also possible.
These examples show why “15% tip-out” and “3% tip-out” cannot be compared without knowing what the percentage is applied to.
What is a normal server tip-out percentage?

There is no single percentage that applies everywhere. Tip-out can depend on the restaurant, role, shift, sales mix and local law. Ask which employees participate, which sales or tips form the calculation base, and whether managers or supervisors are excluded where required.

In the United States, federal rules distinguish between traditional tip pools and nontraditional tip pools. State and local rules can be more protective. The calculator performs arithmetic only; it cannot determine whether a workplace policy is lawful.
Why track tip-out after every shift?

One shift tells you what you took home. A consistent record shows whether a job, role or weekday actually pays your time well. Record gross tips, tip-out, hours and wages together so that changes in the workplace or schedule remain visible.
TipHaven keeps those numbers together on your iPhone and calculates net tips, total earnings and true hourly earnings for every shift.
From one calculation to a useful history
Keep the result, not the mental math.
Track every shift, compare jobs and days, and see where your time pays best.
Is tip-out calculated before or after taxes?
Tip-out is part of the shift earnings calculation, while taxes are handled separately through payroll and tax reporting. This calculator shows amounts before taxes.
Should I enter cash and card tips together?
Yes. Enter total gross tips before tip-out. If your workplace applies different rules to cash and card tips, calculate each portion separately.
What if I tip out different roles at different rates?
Calculate each tip-out separately and add them together, or enter the total as a fixed amount for the final net-tip calculation.
Does this calculator save my earnings?
No. It runs in your browser and does not save or send the values you enter.

How to split a tip pool by hours worked
person’s share = distributable tips × (person’s hours ÷ total hours)

First subtract any documented amount that is removed before distribution. Divide the remaining pool by total eligible hours to find the value of one worked hour. Multiply that rate by each person’s eligible hours.
Why the final cents may differ

Currency is paid to two decimal places, but proportional shares often contain fractions of a cent. This calculator rounds each share and assigns any remaining cent difference to the largest unrounded shares so the final distribution matches the pool exactly.
Use the rules your workplace actually follows

Some workplaces split tips equally, by hours, by points or by role. This calculator handles proportional hours. Under U.S. federal rules, eligibility for mandatory tip pools depends partly on whether the employer takes a tip credit, and managers and supervisors generally may not receive other employees’ pooled tips. State rules may be more protective.

Should a tip pool be split equally or by hours?
Use the method established by your workplace. An hours-based split gives a larger share to people who worked more eligible hours.
Can I subtract a house tip-out first?
Yes. Enter the amount as a deduction only if that matches the documented distribution method that applies to the pool.
Does this decide who is legally eligible?
No. It only performs the arithmetic. Eligibility depends on the workplace and applicable law.
